_comment: English bodies for agno (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. No extraSections in source; sections/sectionTitles omitted. providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access: Multi-model access (each vendor's API and local lines, not itemized); the positioning line is "The self-driving agent platform" (official repo description) — two layers: a framework library + a control plane (AgentOS).
axes.runtime: A Python framework + the AgentOS runtime: the library side defines agents/teams/workflows, the control-plane side runs and observes them. GitHub agno-agi/agno 42,981 stars, last push 2026-10-30 (API verified, highly active); releases are frequent (v3.1.12, 2026-10-29); the site changelog's latest entry is 2026-10-30.
axes.local_files: The library and AgentOS can be self-hosted ("runs in your cloud", official wording); the hosted control plane is a separate product surface (os.agno.com).
axes.background: The AgentOS control plane carries resident-running and observability semantics by itself (agents run inside the plane, tasks can be scheduled); pure library usage is ordinary in-process calls.
axes.tools: Built-in tool / knowledge-base / memory component lines (framework-native memory + knowledge components are the selling point); MCP support status not itemized.
axes.context: Built-in memory and knowledge components (agent memory, knowledge/RAG surfaces) are part of the product narrative; details not itemized.
axes.permissions: The control plane holds credentials and runs agents and tools — authentication and isolation of a self-hosted plane are operational duties; on the hosted surface (os.agno.com) data sits vendor-side.
axes.fit: Fits: wanting "framework + control plane" as one (run + observe + schedule), the Python ecosystem, selections that need frequent releases and active maintenance. Does not fit: wanting only a thin library without a plane, the TS ecosystem (Python-first).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).

related: Same-category contrast: LangGraph gives you graphs and state mechanisms so you build the plane; Agno hands you the plane (AgentOS) directly — build vs. given.
Same-category contrast: Letta's memory is the agent-self-edited core (server form); Agno's memory is a framework-built-in component (plane-observability form).
Cross-category contrast: Dify builds agent apps visually with low-code; Agno defines agents in code and hands them to a plane to run — a boundary sample between automation and framework.
